title: U.S. House · Massachusetts's 1st District
area: Western Massachusetts, including Springfield, Pittsfield, and the Berkshires

context.text: Incumbent Richard Neal defeated Jeromie Whalen, a Belchertown schoolteacher, in the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary, 55.2% to 44.8%. No Republican candidate appeared on the primary ballot.

priorities.text: "I've fought tirelessly for policies that make a difference for hard-working families and future generations: fairer taxes, affordable and accessible healthcare, taking on climate change, preserving Social Security, and more."

Campaign statement: fighting "back against Donald Trump and Republicans' reckless budget that slashes healthcare for working families to give tax breaks to the wealthy and add trillions to the deficit."

positions.summary: In an official statement on the Medicare and Medicaid anniversary, said Democrats will keep fighting to protect and strengthen both programs and expand access to care, and criticized Medicaid cuts.
positions.quote: Democrats will continue fighting to protect and strengthen these programs, lower costs, expand access to care

positions.summary: With Sen. Wyden, opposed giving the President new authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent in the Sanctioning Russia Act and criticized the administration's existing tariffs.
positions.quote: we cannot support awarding even more tariff power to Trump.

positions.summary: In a statement on House passage of a War Powers Resolution on Iran, said the power to declare war rests with Congress.
positions.quote: the House reminded the President and the nation who the power to declare war rests with, and that is with Congress.

record.text: Serves as Ranking Member of the House Ways and Means Committee.
Statement on House passage of a War Powers Resolution following U.S. strikes in Iran, saying Congress "reminded the President and the nation who the power to declare war rests with."

candidates.name: Nadia Milleron

priorities.text: Eliminating federal income tax on earnings under $100,000.
priorities.quote: Nadia supports eliminating federal income tax on earnings under $100,000.

priorities.text: Removing corporate insurers from health care.
priorities.quote: Nadia supports kicking corporate insurance out of healthcare.

priorities.text: Bringing manufacturing, including essential goods such as medicines, back to the U.S.
priorities.quote: Nadia supports strong manufacturing with real standards and producing more of what we consume, especially essential goods like medicines, right here in the U.S.

priorities.text: A pledge to serve no more than three terms.
priorities.quote: Nadia supports a pledge for 3 terms—not 17.

positions.summary: Her campaign Policies page says she would cap rents and ban corporate speculators from buying neighborhood housing.
positions.quote: We will lower living costs by capping runaway rents, banning corporate speculators from buying up local neighborhoods, and directing federal funding straight into community housing developments.

candidates.researchNotes: From the Policies page of her campaign site (written in the third person). Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey not checked (Ballotpedia returned a bot challenge).

statements.quote: Nadia supports kicking corporate insurance out of healthcare.
Nadia will work to stop price gouging, close corporate tax loopholes, and use that revenue to lower costs for working people.
U.S. tax dollars are funding the destruction of Palestinian lives, and that is not only a moral failure but a strategic one.
statements.context: On her campaign Policies page, under "Human Rights"
